title: Code quality: formatting, linting, and tests

spans.text: Code quality improves when checks are repeatable and automated. A formatter applies consistent layout; a linter flags suspicious patterns and style issues; a type checker reasons about annotated types; tests verify behavior. These tools complement one another and do not prove a program is bug-free.

spans.code:
python -m unittest discover -s tests
ruff check .
ruff format --check .

spans.text:
A PRACTICAL CHECK LOOP

1. Write a small test for expected behavior and important edge cases.
2. Run the tests; fix failures rather than weakening a useful assertion.
3. Run a linter and formatter check, then review the diff.
4. Re-run the checks before sharing the change.

Keep tests deterministic: control time, randomness, environment, and external services where practical. Put development tools in the project's documented development setup so another person can reproduce the checks. Start with a manageable set of rules, then tighten it as the project grows.

spans.title: Tools have different jobs
spans.text: Formatting is not linting, and passing lint or type checks is not a substitute for tests. A passing test suite only covers the cases it actually exercises.
